disposition_reason: Table 1 gives fresh-weight mean aluminium, arsenic, cadmium and lead for 13 Jamaican-grown food crops including ackee and banana.

study.design: Market and farm survey of Jamaican-grown food crops with dietary risk assessment
study.method: Acid digestion (HCl:HNO3) and flame/graphite furnace AAS with Zeeman correction; INAA (SLOWPOKE-2) for Al, As, Cd; lead by AAS only
study.lod_text: AAS fresh-weight LODs: Al 0.722-15.0, As 0.007-0.150, Cd 0.001-0.020, Pb 0.003-0.065 mg/kg; INAA LODs: Al 0.5, As 0.0005, Cd 0.01 mg/kg
study.qa: About 10% duplicates (<15% difference); reagent blanks; CRMs NIST 1573a tomato leaves, NIST 1547 peach leaves, IAEA 336 lichen with recoveries within 10%

findings.group: Jamaican-grown, markets and farms island-wide, all samples
findings.notes: Edible portion, washed and peeled; dried at <=60 C and reported on fresh weight; ackee aril analysed fresh. Number of samples per crop not stated. AAS (Al flame, As/Cd/Pb graphite furnace) and INAA (Al, As, Cd); the table does not say which method each mean comes from.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Estimated daily intake, THQ, HI and arsenic target cancer risk per crop (US EPA method), FAO food balance sheet intakes for Jamaica 2013
regulatory_or_exposure.value: All THQ and HI < 1; arsenic TCR < 1E-4

unresolved: Number of samples per crop and collection dates are not reported.
Abstract gives aluminium 4.25-93.12 and cadmium 0.015-0.420 mg/kg, but Table 1 and the text give aluminium from 2.58 (pumpkin) and cadmium up to 0.286 mg/kg (turnip); Table 1 values used.
Some cell means may be below the upper end of the stated AAS LOD ranges (e.g. cabbage As 0.001 vs As LOD 0.007-0.150 by AAS); which method produced each value is not stated, so no flag set.
Arsenic is total arsenic; no speciation.
